From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Post-call: Model fit recap & HelixPoint eval request

Hi Eloise — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs (from our call)
- Use case: clinical triage summarization + high-precision redaction of PHI before downstream routing.
- Target latency: 300–500ms per request at p95 for 1–2k qps baseline (expected pilot traffic low).
- Primary success metric: extractive recall of key fields (patient name, DOB, med codes) > 96% + false positive rate for labeled PHI < 1.5%.
- Secondary: summary coherence and hallucination rate (qualitative spot-checks).

Recommended eval setup from Redwood
- Models to test: 1) Llama-2-70B-chat (FP16) as baseline; 2) Mistral-Instruct-70B (quantized 4-bit) for cost/latency tradeoff; 3) Redwood-distilled-13B (fast, low-cost) as a fallback.
- Prompt set: we’ll run your 1k sample (attached) through the triage prompt + two few-shot variants. We recommend preserving original clinical note order and adding a redaction task as a separate step to measure precision/recall independently.
- Dataset format: CSV (attached sample) with columns: id, raw_text, labels_json (ner spans), acceptance_criteria. See priyom’s note below for exact field expectations.
- Scoring: exact-span match for PHI types (precision/recall/F1), and BLEU/ROUGE-lite for summary overlap plus human spot-checks for hallucination.

Security/PII notes
- We discussed a short DPA + access-limited eval workspace for HelixPoint. We can run in Redwood Hosted under a customer-scoped project; if you need on-prem, we can talk Dedicated/Private options but will add lead time.

Next steps (action owners & timeline)
1) Eloise: share 1–2k de-identified sample (or the sample you feel comfortable with) and your scoring rubric — target by Thu 11/26. (attachment: eval_dataset_sample.csv)
2) Redwood (Priyom): provide eval runbook & exact dataset schema + small pre-run to sanity-check format — by Mon 11/30.
3) Eloise + Aditya: 30-min onboarding to walk the eval workspace and results dashboard — propose Wed 12/1 or Thu 12/2.

Attachments: helixpoint_policy_questions.xlsx (security/compliance Qs), eval_dataset_sample.csv (format sample)

If that all looks right, I’ll send a calendar invite for the onboarding slot once you confirm availability.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Aditya — this is a great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) PII & data: We can provide a 1k sample next-day but it will still contain raw PHI. We need confirmation that the hosted eval workspace will not persist unencrypted copies beyond the run and that RBAC will be enforced. I’ve attached our security checklist (see helixpoint_policy_questions.xlsx) — can your security team confirm the items?

2) Scoring priorities: Our product team ranks PHI redaction correctness > recall for extraction (we can tolerate slightly lower recall if precision for redaction is very high). So if you could make precision-weighted scoring the default that would help.

3) Timeline: We’re aiming for a decision by mid-December. Running the 1k sample + two prompt variants and a short human spot-check should be sufficient for the pilot.

I can do the onboarding on 12/2 after 10am PT. Let me know what you need from my side to unblock the eval.

—Eloise

--- Priyom’s Eval Runbook (high-level) ---
1) Ingest format (strict): CSV UTF-8 with columns: id, raw_text, labels_json. labels_json should be string-encoded JSON with array of spans: [{"type":"PHI_NAME","start":12,"end":21}]. Provide a small validation script we’ll run before upload.
2) Workspace: create customer-scoped eval project under HelixPoint; enable RBAC so only Eloise + two HelixPoint reviewers can access results; retention: 30 days by default (we can change if they request).
3) Models & configs to schedule (parallel runs):
   - run_a: Llama-2-70B-chat (fp16, no quant) — baseline
   - run_b: mistral-instruct-70b (4-bit q4) — cost/latency tradeoff
   - run_c: redwood-distilled-13b (int8) — fast, low cost
   - prompt variants: canonical prompt, few-shot with 3 positive examples, few-shot with 3 edge-case negatives
4) Batch sizing / runtime guidance: start with batch=8, max_seq=2048; if we see memory pressure drop to batch=4 for 70B. target throughput for pilot is low; primary goal is signal quality not scale.
5) Scoring scripts: provide automated scorer that computes per-type precision/recall/F1, and aggregate weighted score (weights: redaction_precision=0.5, extraction_recall=0.35, summary_coherence=0.15). We should also surface hallucination flags where model introduces entities not present in source.
6) Human review: route 50 random summaries + redaction outputs to HelixPoint reviewers; collect binary agree/disagree on hallucinatory content.
7) Deliverables: PDF of run results, raw scorer CSV, and access to the interactive eval dashboard (link below).

Links / assets:
- Eval dashboard (internal): https://app.redwood.ai/evals/HP-3391
- Validation script (dropbox): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDefHelixpoint-eval
